name: Rendering Pipeline Architecture
text:
# Rendering Pipeline Architecture


## Overview
Rendering Pipeline Architecture defines the structural organization of GPU stages required to render volumetric data as splatted primitives, managing the transition from 3D point attributes to 2D screen-space accumulation [S1, unofficial]. It solves the problem of correctly handling transparency, occlusion, and attribute interpolation for large point sets by decomposing the rendering task into distinct, hardware-accelerated passes [S1, unofficial]. It differs from [Single-Pass Splat Rendering Pipeline](1254-single-pass-splat-rendering-pipeline.md) by separating concerns (depth, color, normalization) to ensure correct blending, and from [Splat Attributes Pass](1066-splat-attributes-pass.md) by explicitly handling weight normalization in a dedicated final stage rather than embedding it in attribute computation.

## Shared principles
The family shares the fundamental mechanism of treating volumetric data as a set of geometric or parametric primitives that are transformed and rasterized [S1, S3, S4, unofficial].

1.  **Primitive Representation:** The volume is decomposed into primitives. These may be explicit geometric shapes (cubes, cells, splats) or implicit functions sampled via texture hardware [S1, S3, S4, unofficial]. Each primitive $k$ is defined by its position $\mathbf{p}_k$, density/extinction coefficient $g_k$ or $\rho_k$, and a reconstruction kernel $h$ (typically a Gaussian) [S1, unofficial][S6, unofficial][S10, abstract only, unofficial].
2.  **Transformation:** Primitives are transformed from volume space to screen space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix or specific factorizations (e.g., [shear-warp](#24-shear-warp.md)) [S2, S3, S4, unofficial]. For perspective projections, the kernel shape may be distorted (e.g., [EWA splatting](#1069-ewa-splatting.md)) to account for foreshortening [S6, unofficial][S10, abstract only, unofficial].
3.  **Rasterization:** The transformed primitives are projected onto the 2D image plane. This step leverages hardware-accelerated scan-conversion, depth testing, and blending [S1, S2, S3, S4, unofficial]. The contribution of a voxel $D$ to a screen point $(x,y)$ is determined by the [footprint function](#4731-footprint-function-mechanism.md) $F(x,y)$, which is the integral of the 3D kernel along the view direction [S2, unofficial][S6, unofficial][S10, abstract only, unofficial]:
    $$ F(x,y) = \int h(x-x_D, y-y_D, z) \, dz $$
    The intensity written to the pixel is modulated by the voxel density:
    $$ P(x,y) = \text{weight}(x,y) \cdot \rho(D) $$
    where $\text{weight}(x,y) = F(x-x_D, y-y_D)$ [S10, abstract only, unofficial].
4.  **[Compositing](#2436-compositing.md):** Contributions are accumulated to form the final image. This is typically done using [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) in back-to-front or front-to-back order to handle transparency correctly [S1, S2, S3, unofficial][S7]. [Splatting](#23-splatting.md) compositing is performed along sheets (all pixels at once for a set of voxels), whereas [ray-casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) composites along rays (one sample at a time) [S10, abstract only, unofficial].
5.  **Hardware [Acceleration](#18-acceleration.md):** Most methods in this family rely on GPU rasterization pipelines for performance, enabling real-time interactivity [S1, S2, S3, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Splat Attributes Pass](1066-splat-attributes-pass.md)
Computes per-pixel geometric and photometric attributes for point-sampled primitives by evaluating their intersection with the view ray. It solves the problem of correctly occluding back faces of spherical splats while accumulating weighted color, normal, and opacity data into a G-buffer. It differs from [Single-Pass Splat Rendering Pipeline](1254-single-pass-splat-rendering-pipeline.md) by explicitly separating attribute accumulation into a dedicated pass writing to intermediate textures, and from [Three-Pass GPU Point Rendering Pipeline](2837-three-pass-gpu-point-rendering-pipeline.md) by relying on fragment-level depth testing against a pre-computed depth buffer rather than explicit tile-based sorting.

### [Single-Pass Splat Rendering Pipeline](1254-single-pass-splat-rendering-pipeline.md)
Combines splat and mesh rendering components to enable [high-quality shader](#10218-single-atomic-high-quality-robust-variant-hqs1r.md) effects (reflection, refraction) in a single rendering pass. It avoids [multi-pass blending](#6724-multi-pass-blending.md) artifacts and reduces memory/workload by interpolating attributes in object space rather than screen space.

### [Three-Pass GPU Point Rendering Pipeline](2837-three-pass-gpu-point-rendering-pipeline.md)
Separates depth occlusion, color accumulation, and normalization into distinct [rendering stages](#1318-volume-rendering-pipeline.md). It solves the problem of correctly blending overlapping splats with varying filter weights on standard graphics hardware without requiring complex software sorting. Unlike [Single-Pass Splat Rendering Pipeline](1254-single-pass-splat-rendering-pipeline.md), it uses an intermediate depth buffer to resolve occlusion before accumulating color. It differs from [Splat Attributes Pass](1066-splat-attributes-pass.md) by explicitly handling the normalization of accumulated weights in a final dedicated pass.

## Background
Origin: The architectural [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) of splat rendering into multi-pass pipelines emerged from the need to handle complex lighting and occlusion on early GPU hardware [S1, unofficial]. The specific three-pass approach for point clouds was detailed in early 2000s literature on [hardware-accelerated point rendering](#8433-opengl-point-rendering-for-isosurfaces.md) [S1, unofficial]. The single-pass elevation map approach was introduced to support [continuous attribute interpolation](#1246-continuous-attribute-interpolation.md) for high-fidelity visualization [S1, unofficial].
